away.name: Alex Nedeljkovic
away.news: After a back-to-back, the Sharks will turn to Nedeljkovic on Tuesday following a 3-1 loss to the Toronto Maple Leafs last night. Nedeljkovic has only started three of nine games to start the season, but has been more consistent than counterpart Yaroslav Askarov. The 30-year-old Nedeljkovic has a solid 2.20 GAA and .920 SV% in three games (2-0-1). Still, the Sharks enter Tuesday's contest as sizeable +179 road underdogs against a Montreal Canadiens team that has scored four or more goals in three straight games (2-1-0).

home.name: Jakub Dobes
home.news: After a breakout 2025-26 season that continued with an impressive postseason run, Dobes has struggled early in 2026-27. The 25-year-old Czech goalie has allowed five or more goals in three of four games, giving Jacob Fowler more action in recent weeks. Dobes has an ugly 4.63 GAA and .842 SV% in four games (1-2-1). Still, the Canadiens enter Tuesday's contest as significant -202 home favourites over a San Jose Sharks team coming off a 3-1 loss last night to the Toronto Maple Leafs.

away.name: Scott Wedgewood
away.news: Wedgewood's tremendous 2025-26 season, posting a 2.02 GAA and .921 SV% in 45 appearances (31-6-6), should at least earn him a near timeshare by season's end, but Colorado has leaned heavily on Mackenzie Blackwood to start the 2026-27 season. That said, Wedgewood will tend the twine on Tuesday in the tail end of a back-to-back, his third start in 10 games this season. The 34-year-old Wedgewood has a 2.40 GAA and .902 SV% in two games (1-0-1). Colorado enters Tuesday's action as slight +100 road underdogs against a New Jersey Devils team coming off a 4-2 loss to the Washington Capitals.

home.name: Jake Allen
home.news: After trading Jacob Markstrom in the offseason, the Devils are rolling with a makeshift goalie tandem of Jake Allen and Nico Daws. The 36-year-old Allen has started 35 or fewer games in six of his past seven seasons, and his 2026-27 start hasn't been overly reassuring. Allen has allowed four or more goals in three of five games (3-2-0), posting a 3.18 GAA and .876 SV%. Still, the Devils enter Tuesday's contest as slight -110 home favourites against a Colorado Avalanche team that lost 3-2 last night to the Philadelphia Flyers.

away.name: Lukas Dostal
away.news: The Ducks fell 5-2 to the New York Rangers last night, extending their losing streak to three games, and hope to return to the win column on Tuesday when they turn to Dostal to tend the twine. Dostal has had an up-and-down start to the 2026-27 season and is coming off a poor performance, allowing four goals on 22 shots (.818 SV%) in a 4-2 loss to the Boston Bruins. The 26-year-old Czech goalie had a 3.17 GAA and .882 SV% in six games this season (3-3-0). The Ducks enter Tuesday's action as +134 road underdogs against a New York Islanders team coming off an impressive 4-1 win over the Toronto Maple Leafs.

home.name: Ilya Sorokin
home.news: Sorokin was excellent in his most recent outing, building on a strong start to the 2026-27 season by saving 28 of 29 shots (.966 SV%) in a 4-1 win over the Toronto Maple Leafs. The 31-year-old goalie has allowed two or fewer goals in five of six games this season (4-2-0), posting a tremendous 1.68 GAA and .940 SV%. The Islanders enter Tuesday's contest as -149 home favourites against an Anaheim Ducks team that has been outscored 13-6 during a three-game losing streak (0-3-0).

home.name: Logan Thompson
home.news: Thompson has quietly become one of the NHL's most consistent and reliable goalies over the past several seasons, coming off consecutive 31-win campaigns. The 29-year-old goalie has had some ups and downs to start the 2026-27 season, but is coming off a tremendous performance, saving 29 of 31 shots (.935 SV%) in a 4-2 win over the New Jersey Devils. Thompson has a 2.69 GAA and .910 SV% in six games this season (4-2-0). The Capitals enter Tuesday's contest as -154 home favourites against a low-scoring Los Angeles Kings team that has been outscored 25-12 through six games this season (0-4-2).

away.name: Anthony Stolarz
away.news: Sergei Bobrovsky led the Maple Leafs to a 3-1 win over the San Jose Sharks last night, and they will look to win consecutive games for the first time this season, turning to Stolarz on Tuesday against the Columbus Blue Jackets. The Maple Leafs have relied on Bobrovsky for seven of 10 games to start the season, as Stolarz has struggled in recent outings, allowing four or more goals in consecutive games (1-1-0). The 32-year-old Stolarz has a 3.32 GAA and .875 SV% in three games (2-1-0). The Maple Leafs enter Tuesday's contest as +133 road underdogs against a Blue Jackets team that has scored fewer than two goals in its last three games (1-1-0).

home.name: Jet Greaves
home.news: Greaves is coming off his first shutout of the season, an exceptional 29-save performance in a 1-0 overtime win over the New York Rangers. It was the first time Greaves had allowed fewer than three goals through four starts this season. The 25-year-old goalie has a 2-2-0 record, a 2.58 GAA, and a .905 SV%. The Blue Jackets enter Tuesday's contest as -150 home favourites against a Toronto Maple Leafs team that snapped a two-game losing streak last night with a 3-1 win over the San Jose Sharks.

away.name: Stuart Skinner
away.news: Impressive early-season performances from Stuart Skinner and Clay Stevenson made Connor Hellebuyck's (suspension) absence an afterthought, but recent struggles are keeping Winnipeg's crease uncertain. Skinner is coming off a season-worst performance, allowing four goals on 28 shots (.857 SV%) in a 4-3 overtime loss to the Chicago Blackhawks. The 27-year-old goalie has a 2.76 GAA and .906 SV% in five games (3-0-2). The Jets enter Tuesday's contest as +128 road underdogs against a St. Louis Blues team that has lost five of their last seven (2-4-1).

home.name: Joel Hofer
home.news: Hofer delivered a dazzling 25-save shutout in the Blues' season opener, validating Head Coach Jim Montgomery's decision to bench veteran Jordan Binnington, but Hofer has struggled since. The 26-year-old Hofer is coming off a season-worst performance, allowing five goals on 39 shots (.872 SV%) in a 5-4 loss to the St. Louis Blues. He has a 2.43 GAA and .906 SV% in five games (2-2-1). The Blues enter Tuesday's contest as -142 home favourites against a Winnipeg Jets team that has lost three of their last four (1-2-1).

away.name: Jeremy Swayman
away.news: Jeremy Swayman had a miserable 2024-25 season after signing a massive eight-year contract extension, posting an ugly 3.11 GAA and .892 SV% in 58 games (22-29-7). The organization had concerns about the contract, but he followed it up with a solid 2025-26 season, posting a 2.71 GAA and .907 SV% in 55 games (31-18-4). Now, the 27-year-old goalie seems to be continuing his upward trajectory, opening the season with an outstanding 1.85 GAA and .934 SV% in seven games (6-1-0). The Bruins enter Tuesday's action as +146 road underdogs against a Dallas Stars team with points in five of their last six games (4-1-1).

home.name: Jake Oettinger
home.news: The Stars have struggled offensively at times to start the season, but can attribute a winning 4-3-1 record to the outstanding play of Jake Oettinger. In six games this season (3-2-1), the 27-year-old Oettinger has already posted three shutouts, with an outstanding 1.00 GAA and .952 SV%. He stopped all 19 shots in his previous game, a 4-0 win over the Chicago Blackhawks. The Stars enter Tuesday's contest as -162 home favourites against a Boston Bruins team riding a league-best five-game winning streak.

away.name: Jesper Wallstedt
away.news: Wallstedt has been busy with Filip Gustavsson (hip) sidelined and will return to the crease for the ninth time in Minnesota's first 10 games. That said, the increased playing time hasn't hindered the 23-year-old Wallstedt, who has a dazzling 1.99 GAA and .922 SV% in eight games (1-1-0). Still, Minnesota enters Tuesday's matchup as slight +116 road underdogs against a 6-1-1 Edmonton Oilers team that is clicking offensively (4.63 GF/GP).

home.name: Devon Levi
home.news: The Oilers have struggled between the pipes in recent seasons, but Devon Levi's play has been encouraging early in the 2026-27 season. That said, Levi is coming off his first loss as an Oiler, allowing three goals on 24 shots (.875 SV%) in a 4-2 loss to the Utah Mammoth. The 24-year-old goalie has allowed two or fewer goals in three of five games this season (4-1-0), posting a 2.83 GAA and .898 SV%. The Oilers enter Tuesday's contest as -129 home favourites against a 6-2-1 Minnesota Wild team.

away.name: Daniil Tarasov
away.news: Tarasov has been exceptional in limited action this season and appears to be getting more playing time as a result, as he will tend the twine for the third time in Detroit's last five games. The 27-year-old goalie saved 17 of 18 shots (.944 SV%) in his most recent outing, a 2-1 win over the Philadelphia Flyers. He has a 0.80 GAA and a .965 SV% in three appearances (1-0-1).

home.name: Philipp Grubauer
home.news: Seattle is off to a solid 5-3-1 start this season and has received encouraging goaltending from Grubauer, who has never lived up to being the team's number-one goalie. That said, Grubauer will hope to bounce back after a season-worst performance in which he allowed four goals on 35 shots (.886 SV%) in a 4-3 overtime loss to the Tampa Bay Lightning. The 34-year-old German goalie has a 2.71 GAA and .910 SV% in five games (2-1-1). The Kraken enter Tuesday's contest as +102 home underdogs against a Detroit Red Wings team on a two-game winning streak.

away.name: Pyotr Kochetkov
away.news: Hurricanes Head Coach Rod Brind'Amour started Brandon Bussi in the first two games of the season, but has leaned a bit more heavily on Kochetkov in recent games. The 27-year-old goalie returns to the crease on Tuesday for his sixth start in his last nine games and, deservedly, after posting a tremendous undefeated 5-0-0 record with a 1.78 GAA and .912 SV%. The Hurricanes enter Tuesday's action as enormous -294 road favourites against a Vancouver Canucks team that has scored two or fewer goals in seven consecutive games (0-6-1).

away.name: Andrei Vasilevskiy
away.news: Tampa Bay is on a hot 6-1-0 run, and they've done it without needing Vasilevskiy, the reigning Vezina Trophy winner, to be spectacular. Vasilevskiy has uncharacteristically allowed three goals in each of his last three games (2-1-0). The 32-year-old goalie has a 2.53 GAA and .886 SV% in six games this season (4-2-0). Tampa Bay enters Tuesday's contest as slight -108 road favourites against a Vegas Golden Knights team that has outscored opponents 17-6 in their last three games (3-0-0).

home.name: Carter Hart
home.news: The Golden Knights have rotated goalies in recent games, but they will turn to Hart on Tuesday against the Tampa Bay Lightning. Hart was excellent in his most recent outing, saving 28 of 30 shots (.933 SV%) in a 6-2 win over the Calgary Flames. The 28-year-old Canadian goalie has a 2.35 GAA and .911 SV% in six games (4-2-0). The Golden Knights enter Tuesday's matchup as slight -102 home underdogs against a Tampa Bay Lightning team that is 6-1-0 in their last seven games.
